about: The icons of Christ in the edit. Each is a faithful photograph of a flat work, marked Public domain on Wikimedia Commons, where each was fetched on 2026-11-22 (the page is given). Seven were made between the 6th and the 17th century. Two are late: 'pantocrator19' and 'golden' are the work of unnamed Russian painters of the late 19th or the early 20th century, so their makers are not known to have died before 1900; Commons marks both Public domain, and that is all this file claims for them. None is held in Greece or Italy, so none is on the heritage list (lib/marketing/heritagePictures.ts). The first is the app's own icon (public/shop/media/christ-pantocrator-mounted.jpg and public/icons/prayer/christ-pantocrator.v2.jpg show the same work); the others are not in the app. 'eyes' is where His eyes are in the fetched file, read off by hand: the eye at the viewer's left first. 'halo' is the halo's circle: centre x, y and radius. 'fetched_width' is the width Wikimedia served; the eyes are in that file's pixels.

sinai.what: Christ Pantocrator, encaustic on panel, 6th century
sinai.used: the figure that rises in the dome; the question; the runs of faces

zlatye.what: The Saviour of the Golden Hair, early 13th century

novgorod.what: The Holy Face (the Saviour Not Made by Hands), Novgorod, 12th century

ushakov.what: The Holy Face, by Simon Ushakov, 1658

pantocrator19.what: Christ Pantocrator, tempera on wood, late 19th century
pantocrator19.used: the figure that stands first in the dome; the second shot ("and"); the runs of faces

vysotsky.what: Christ Pantocrator from the Vysotsky tier, Byzantine, 1387 to 1395
vysotsky.used: the third shot ("the life") and the shot beneath the first run of faces; the runs of faces

rublev.what: The Saviour, from the Zvenigorod tier, by Andrei Rublev, about 1410

yaroe.what: The Saviour of the Fiery Eye, mid 14th century

golden.what: Christ Pantocrator on a chased gold ground, tempera on wood, Russia, late 19th or early 20th century
